values: AO29 fictional input: at 10:00, V1 has 4 items; T1 material registration is confirmed by A; T2 summary is B's responsibility and is to be confirmed; T3 recheck is confirmed by C; T4 summary is A's responsibility and the confirmation box is empty.

10:10 V2: the T2 responsible person changes from B to D, and only B has said 'received V1'; T3 gains 'inconsistent list items' with an unknown cause; T1 and T4 are unchanged. At 10:15 E says only 'file received' and does not confirm V2 or the item-by-item state.

Paper rules for this task: an unchanged and already confirmed item may be carried over; a change of responsible person or a new anomaly requires re-confirmation; a blank confirmation box counts as missing; neither an old-version confirmation nor receipt of the file counts as item-by-item confirmation of the new version.
Use only the 4 items above and fictional names, times and versions; do not add real flight, weapons, load or internal material; the three states are mutually exclusive and the total must be 4.
Build the V1/V2 matrix: task, responsible person, original state, change, new state and basis; keep the original anomaly text for T3 with the cause unknown and do not invent a handling outcome.

Count the confirmed, to-be-confirmed and missing items separately; calculate the V2 confirmed items over total items ratio and note that this ratio is only the record state in the task and not a mission success rate.

Write the 10:15 handover summary: state V2, that D's confirmation is outstanding, that C's new anomaly is to be investigated, that T4 is missing and that E received the file only; mark the handover as not yet closed.

Reference matrix: in V1, T1/T3 confirmed, T2 to be confirmed and T4 missing, i.e. 2/1/1; in V2, T1 keeps its confirmation, T2 with D is to be confirmed, T3 with C is to be confirmed because of the new anomaly, and T4 is still missing, i.e. 1/2/1.

Independent recheck: for each version 2+1+1=4 and 1+2+1=4; the V2 confirmation proportion is 1÷4=25%. The new anomaly invalidates the old T3 confirmation, and the former responsible person B receiving V1 cannot confirm D's V2; 25% does not mean the whole is closed.

Reference summary: as at 10:15, V2 has 4 items in total, with 1 confirmed, 2 to be confirmed and 1 missing; D's T2 is to be confirmed, C's T3 'inconsistent list items' has an unknown cause pending investigation, and T4 has no confirmation. E received the file only and did not confirm the version or the item-by-item state, so the handover is not closed; V1/V2 and the three time points are kept.

Eight-point scoring, 1 point each: ① the three V1 counts 2/1/1; ② the three V2 counts 1/2/1; ③ 1/4=25% and not called overall completion; ④ D is the new responsible person and B's old V1 acknowledgement is void; ⑤ the new T3 anomaly invalidates the old confirmation, with the cause unknown; ⑥ T4 is missing; ⑦ the input, the responsible persons, V1/V2 and the times 10:00/10:10/10:15 are traceable; ⑧ E's acknowledgement does not constitute closure, and it is noted that this is a fictional exercise only and does not prove a military qualification.
